clauses.reason: The order exempts David D. Caldwell, Special Assistant to the Attorney General, Department of Justice, from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, and fixes the period in its own words: "for a period of one year ending January 31, 1942". The recital says David D. Caldwell had been exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year by Executive Order No. 8312 of December 21, 1939; those earlier orders precede this one and are not events of it. The end is recorded as January 31, 1942 (1942-01-31), inclusive: the exemption runs through that day. The exclusive reading, under which it ends when that day begins, is the alternative. EO 8919, signed October 21, 1941, cites this order by number ("No. 8630 of ") and exempts the same employee again: "I hereby further exempt" ... "for a period of one year ending January 31, 1943". It states no separate effective date, so its signature date is recorded as the event date. It is a later event, not an end: it is a new exemption for a later period and does not revoke, shorten or supersede the exemption in EO 8630.
